commitResults.messageBody: Move file-path handling, task serialization, and task reconstruction out of Ultron so command processing no longer depends on file I/O details. This establishes a dedicated persistence boundary for later Ui, Parser, and TaskList extractions.

Move task storage, indexed access, mutation, and task-count calculation into TaskList. Ultron now delegates collection operations instead of maintaining a separate taskCount variable, while Storage receives an immutable snapshot when saving.

Move the greeting, task rendering, confirmations, errors, and separators into Ui so Ultron focuses on command flow. Preserve existing output while fixing deletion to display the removed task safely, including when it was the last item.

Move command recognition, argument extraction, and task-number parsing into Parser. Ultron now switches on parsed commands and coordinates the existing Ui, TaskList, and Storage components without changing command behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Introduce command pattern for exit and list
commitResults.messageBody: Add an abstract Command base class with ExitCommand and ListCommand, and let Parser construct these simple executable commands. Move command input into Ui to establish the read-parse-execute flow while retaining the existing branch for task-changing commands during the transition.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move mark and unmark into command objects
commitResults.messageBody: Add MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand to own task-number validation, status changes, saving, and feedback. Extend Parser to create command objects for these operations, further reducing command-specific logic in Ultron.
Add DeleteCommand to own task-number validation, removal, persistence, and deletion feedback. Extend Parser to construct it and remove the remaining numbered deletion branch from Ultron.

Move application coordination, commands, model, parser, storage, UI, and exceptions into ultron subpackages while retaining src/main/java as the source root. Move the storage integration check into src/test/java and update its deadline fixture to match the current date format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for internal task invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Document assumptions about task types, task-list indexes, recognised
commands, and displaying newly added tasks.

These assertions help detect programming errors during development without
replacing normal validation and error handling for user input.

Centralize one-based task-number parsing and bounds checks in Command.

Mark, unmark, and delete now share the same validation path and error
handling. This removes duplicated logic and reduces the chance that the
commands diverge when validation changes.

Move saved-symbol lookup into TaskType so storage relies on the enum
rather than recreating its T, D, and E mapping.

This creates a single source of truth for task-type symbols and makes a
future task type less likely to be handled inconsistently.

Express task filtering and storage-line construction as declarative
collection transformations.

This removes temporary mutable collections while keeping matching results
unmodifiable. The updated test protects that existing API contract.

Allow a deadline to move to today or a future date while retaining its
existing time unless a replacement is supplied.

Validate replacement times as 24-hour HHmm values and reject changes that
would create past deadlines. Unit tests protect valid updates and failed
updates leaving the task unchanged.

Support absolute dates with an optional replacement time and positive-day
postponements based on the current deadline date.

Reject non-deadlines, completed deadlines, invalid syntax, and changes that
would leave a deadline in the past. Successful commands save immediately
and show the deadline details before and after the update.

Display original task numbers in find results so users can safely use
those numbers in reschedule commands.

Verify that an existing saved deadline can be rescheduled and restored
without changing the file format. Document both command forms, validation,
and outcomes in the project README and user guide.
